answer: Seed-fork conviction: at enrollment an identity seals a private seed, and the registry writes an anchor binding that seal to one seat. Each epoch a probe follows a random wander across past epochs and is answerable once per seed. A farm cloning one image makes N copies answering the same probe, so the duplicate seal collides and the registry convicts the whole lineage. Re-enrollment is glacier-paced: 30 epochs of cooling plus a seat auction priced by queue depth. Each copy needs its own seed lineage, so attacker cost grows with farm size squared while an honest agent pays one probe per epoch.
